prompts.text: What does a really good conversation with someone you're interested in leave you thinking about afterwards?
Tell me about a time you unexpectedly wanted to hear more of someone's perspective.
We've been talking for an hour and neither of us has mentioned work. What do you think we've been discussing?
Learn what shaped someone's worldview or what they're still trying to figure out?
Attraction can begin with curiosity about how another person sees ordinary situations.
Asking thoughtful follow-up questions is more compelling than arriving with a list of impressive stories.
What's an opinion you've changed because a conversation made you reconsider it?
Describe a person who made an unfamiliar subject feel suddenly fascinating.
You could ask me one question knowing I'd give a thoughtful answer. What would you want to understand?
Talk about the books that changed us or the real-life experiences behind our beliefs?
Which tiny part of your day would you enjoy sharing with someone who's getting to know you?
Recall noticing a person's mood shift through a small change in their usual messages.
We're both free for twenty minutes after a demanding day. What kind of catch-up would feel right?
Exchange the best thing that happened today or the question that's been on our minds?
People sometimes become close through mundane updates that would mean little to anyone else.
Consistency in communication matters more than the length of a message.
How would you describe the difference between wanting company and wanting a distraction?
Tell me about someone who recognised that you needed quiet rather than encouragement.
I mention I'm having a rough week but don't explain why. What would you ask before offering advice?
A peaceful call with comfortable pauses or an animated conversation about something new?
What kind of disagreement can reveal positive qualities about a person?
Describe realising that somebody's opposite opinion came from an experience you hadn't considered.
We have very different ideas about how to spend a free Saturday. How should we choose without either of us resenting it?
Discuss one complicated idea in depth or compare several everyday preferences?
Being able to disagree gently is sometimes more revealing than agreeing enthusiastically.
Two people needn't hold identical opinions to share important values.
How do you prefer someone to tell you they see a situation differently?
Recall a conversation that became easier once both people stopped trying to convince each other.
Our discussion grows more serious than expected. What might you say to check that we're both comfortable?
Ask questions until you understand a disagreement or set it aside and return another day?
What's something about your upbringing that influences how you show care?
Tell me about a small family tradition that you've carried into your own routines.
Our families have different expectations about visiting relatives. What would we need to learn before making plans?
Compare childhood celebrations or the life lessons older relatives taught us?
People can share values while expressing respect in ways that seem unfamiliar to each other.
Meeting someone's family isn't a substitute for learning how they personally think.
Which family story helps explain a quality you're proud to have?
Recall an elder whose relationship advice made more sense once you were older.
I ask why a particular holiday matters to you. Where would you begin the story?
Hear about a person who shaped your childhood or a place that still feels like home?
What helps you decide whether you're comfortable opening up to someone new?
Describe a moment when somebody respected a personal boundary without asking for a justification.
I ask about something you'd rather not discuss yet. How would you want us to handle that moment?
Share a difficult experience slowly across several conversations or keep some stories private until the time feels right?
Trust can deepen when people discover that declining a question doesn't change the atmosphere.
Feeling curious about someone doesn't create a right to every detail of their life.
What sort of reassurance is helpful when you're talking about an uncertain situation?
Recall somebody admitting they didn't know how to respond and still making you feel heard.
We're discussing a sensitive subject and one of us becomes quiet. What check-in would feel considerate?
Be asked whether you want advice or whether you simply want somebody to listen?
Which personal goal would you enjoy hearing somebody explain even if it wasn't one you shared?
Tell me about a person whose quiet ambition surprised you more than an impressive achievement.
We both receive an opportunity in different cities. What questions would help us understand each other's priorities?
Explore someone's long-term hopes or the small routines they use to make progress?
People often disclose their priorities through how they spend ordinary afternoons.
Encouraging another person's growth doesn't require knowing exactly where it will lead.
What kind of work would still interest you if nobody else knew you did it?
Recall deciding not to pursue a goal that once seemed central to your plans.
You could take a year to learn one unfamiliar skill. What would make it worth your time?
Talk about the risks we'd like to take or the commitments we'd rather protect?
What does emotional availability look like in everyday behaviour to you?
Describe someone making time for an important conversation when they could easily have avoided it.
One of us is excited about something while the other is exhausted. How could we make space for both feelings?
Someone who checks in when plans change or someone who explains clearly what they can manage?
The practical habits people keep often show more than the labels they choose for themselves.
Saying you need rest can be a sign of honest communication, not lack of interest.
How can someone show care without turning every concern into a problem to solve?
Recall feeling reassured by a person who followed through on something small.
A conversation ends before we reach an understanding. How would you prefer to revisit it?
An honest update about a busy week or frequent short replies that don't say much?
What belief about relationships have you begun to question as you've grown older?
Tell me about noticing a healthy relationship habit in a couple you know.
Our friends give us two contradictory pieces of dating advice. How might we decide what applies to us?
Discuss what a supportive partnership looks like or explore what healthy independence means?
People can want closeness and still have different needs for solitude or social time.
Compatibility should include space for disagreement without fear of punishment.
Which relationship lesson do you wish people learnt before their first serious dating experience?
Recall realising that a romantic gesture you admired in stories wouldn't suit you in real life.
We find we define loyalty differently. What examples might help us understand each other?
Talk about the relationships we've learnt from or the patterns we'd like to do differently?
What place would you show somebody to help them understand what you value?
Describe a visit somewhere that changed your perspective on your own community.
We each choose one meaningful stop for a shared afternoon. How would you explain yours?
Visit a place tied to childhood memories or explore somewhere connected to a new interest?
A person's favourite locations can reflect comfort, curiosity, history or all three.
The best date location may be somewhere ordinary that gives both people room to talk.
What would somebody misunderstand about your hometown if they only visited the tourist attractions?
Recall learning something about a person from the place they chose to take you.
We have a free morning and no booking. What kind of experience might teach us something new about each other?
Explore an unfamiliar neighbourhood together or revisit a familiar place with fresh questions?
What kind of connection makes you want to see where it leads rather than rush to define it?
Describe a moment you realised you were more interested in someone's character than their first impression.
We've enjoyed getting to know each other but our schedules are changing. What would we need to discuss?
Learn how someone navigates uncertainty or how they celebrate good news?
Meaningful connections can grow gradually when both people are clear about their intentions.
Being direct about what you hope for is kinder than leaving the other person to guess.
What tells you a person is interested in knowing the real you rather than an idealised version?
Recall an ordinary conversation that became memorable because you felt free to be yourself.
We discover we're imagining different directions for the connection. What would respectful honesty look like?
Talk about what we're enjoying right now or what we each need before making a bigger commitment?
